12:57 - Lymphoedema Clinic: HANWELL, Victoria (Nurse Access Role) Entered at: LOROS Hospice
 Lymphoedema Outcomes
   Outcome of Assessment
      Outcome of assessment:  Diagnosis/problem  Lymphoedema to left arm and hand following treatment for Breast cancer.

Thankyou for referring Mrs Wallis, she was seen for assessment at the Lymphoedema Clinic at LOROS on 21/8/25.

I discussed the causes and management of lymphoedema, the importance of a good skin care regime and the  prevention of infection(cellulitis)
Please can you prescribe Epimax cream n a 500 gram pump dispenser for Jane to use as an emollient.

I discussed compression therapy and its role in helping to manage lymphoedema. It aims to  control and reduce the swelling, caused by a build up of lymph fluid.  I have also gone through in clinic a set of specific exercises for her  to  perform.

Jane has consented to sign up to PatientChoice a prescription request and  delivery service, who will contact the practise and request a hosiery prescription.

Once the garments have been delivered to Janes home address, she knows to contact the clinic to book a fitting of hosiery appointment.

Mrs Wallis will be reviewed in clinic in six months time, but knows that she can contact us in the meantime if needed.

We no longer send follow up appointments automatically.....

If I can be  of any further assistance......

 Lymphoedema Assessment 2015
   Demo
      Sexual Orientation: Heterosexual (X766q)
      Disability limitations (Patient's opinion): Not limited by disability NOS (Y166a)
   DX
      Previous/Current medical history:  watery eyes ? due to chemotherapy
      Summary of Diagnosis:  Lymphoedema to left upper limb and dorsum of hand, following treatment for Breast cancer
      Lymphoedema Diagnosis: Lymphoedema due to malignant disease (XaR6u)
   Assessment
      Physical problems/concerns:  Lymphoedema face to face initial assessment, referred by her GP with a history of swelling to her left upper  limb and  hand. I introduced myself, also  in clinic was Michelle HCA.  Likes to be called Jane, has had wide local excision and axillary node clearance in July 2024. Followed by chemo/ radiotherapy which finished in November 2024, Jane voiced that currrently she is cancer free.. She first noticed signs of swelling in her arm about eight weeks ago, she doesnt recall any  triggers. She was seen by her GP who referred her to the clinic.
Jane consented for me  to examine her  on the clnic couch, she is right handed,her stemmer sign is -ve, she has good capillary refill. No evidence of pitting oedema noticed, colour and temperature and sensation appear normal. Skin is intact and well moisturised, no evidence of infection. Subcutaneous tissues are soft and supple,signs of lymphoedema along the  length  of  the arm and the dorsum of the hand
Limb volume measurements were taken and show  an excess of 19% or excess ,;s pf 484mls in the  afffected limb.
I discussed the rationale for compression therapy which Jane is happy to try. From clinic I tried a mediven class1 armsleeve but it was too long, and because she is getting some swelling in the dorsum of her hand, I will also request a glove.. Jane has consented for me to sign her  up to PatientChoice
I have explained that garments should be worn daily and removed at night and moisturised. I have also  gone through contraindications/side effects of compression garments..
I have asked her to telephone clinic when the garments arrive and make a fitting of hosiery appointment
Plan
I will write to her GP 
Sign Jane up  to PatientChoice and request garments
Jane will book a FOH appointment when she receives the garments
To return as follow up in six months
